So the the Hilo wild and scenic legislation that we've introduced is really an effort to preserve what is most unique about this watershed. There are so many parts of the Colorado River watershed now where The rivers aren't so much. They're not natural living rivers anymore. And if you just go downstream to Arizona, once you hit some of those dams, the Hilo River is largely dewatered. It's completely tamed. And it's more of a ditch than a river at this point. And the Upper Gila, the San Francisco, still has this really dynamic hydrology that has been lost throughout most of the Colorado River watershed. And because of that dynamism, you have these amazing riparian forests with Arizona, Sycamore and Cottonwoods. You have these incredible you know, bird species that don't really show up anywhere, you know, this far north of Mexico, except for the Hila. And it's because of that natural system.
